record.original_question: Does every connected d-regular graph admit a signing sigma of its edges such that the signed adjacency matrix has spectral radius at most 2*sqrt(d - 1)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 13 (Bilu-Linial [18]). Every connected d-regular graph G has a signature σ with spectral radius at most 2√(d − 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signing of a finite simple graph G = (V, E) is a function σ: E → {−1, +1}. The signed adjacency matrix A_σ is the symmetric V × V matrix whose (u, v)-entry equals σ({u, v}) if {u, v} ∈ E and 0 otherwise. Its spectral radius is the maximum absolute value of its eigenvalues.

Prove or disprove: for every integer d ≥ 2 and every connected d-regular graph G, there exists a signing σ of the edges of G such that the spectral radius of A_σ is at most 2√(d − 1).
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is established for bipartite graphs by Marcus, Spielman, and Srivastava (Interlacing Families I, Annals of Mathematics 2015), which yielded bipartite Ramanujan graphs of every degree. The full conjecture for arbitrary connected d-regular graphs remains open.

status_evidence.title: Interlacing Families I: Bipartite Ramanujan Graphs of All Degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Marcus, Spielman, Srivastava proved existence of signings achieving spectral radius ≤ 2√(d−1) for bipartite d-regular graphs via interlacing families.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture resolved in the bipartite case.

status_evidence.title: Lifts, discrepancy and nearly optimal spectral gap (Bilu-Linial)
status_evidence.snippet: Bilu and Linial proved every d-regular graph has a signature with spectral radius O(√d (log d)^{3/2}); the tight 2√(d−1) bound is conjectured.
status_evidence.claim: Original conjecture; weaker polylog bound proved, full bound conjectured.
